speaker: Doctor
text: That is surprising given the genetic panel was normal; PML is typically caused by a severe immunosuppression, not a hereditary ataxia. Could you tell me if you are currently taking medications for HIV, have you received chemotherapy recently, or have you been prescribed high-dose steroids? Also, do you have a known history of autoimmune disorders like Multiple Sclerosis?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that description; the "drunk" gait and unilateral clumsiness are classic signs of cerebellar involvement. Since the MRI suggests PML but the genetic panel for hereditary ataxias was normal, I need to understand your immune status better. Have you ever been diagnosed with HIV, been treated for cancer, or taken high-dose steroids or other immunosuppressants recently?

Given the negative HIV status and normal blood work, PML is unlikely; the multifocal demyelinating lesions on your MRI could actually represent a variant of Multiple Sclerosis or a paraneoplastic syndrome. Have you noticed any new sensory changes like numbness, or any endocrine issues like unexplained weight gain or fatigue? Additionally, have you had any recent malignancies or undergone a CT scan of your abdomen or chest recently?

Could you describe if these lesions have appeared in multiple distinct areas of your brain or spinal cord? Additionally, have you experienced any visual disturbances like double vision or loss of vision in one eye?

text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
